title: The Oath of the Glass Steppe Anew
premise: Emrys Almeida, a mercenary bound by oath to a god that has not spoken in a decade, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names that were never given. When she discovers tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies, she is seized by the prophecy itself and carried to the court of King Aldric, whose crown is worn by something else entirely: a parasite of glass and memory called the Regent. To free Aldric and save the free cities from the usurper's advancing armies, Emrys must break her own oath, trading the god's protection for the truth of what happened the night the god went silent—a truth her guild masters buried and her own memories hold. In the end she shatters the Regent at the cost of the god's final breath, chooses loyalty to people over truth to powers, and rebuilds the ledgers as a record of debts forgiven rather than debts owed.
about_author: Freya Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist who spent seven years cataloguing mercenary company records in coastal free cities before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about paperwork, oaths, and the quiet violence of institutions.

chapters.title: The Ledger Opens Both Ways
chapters.summary: Emrys Almeida audits the Vellum Guild's night inventory, cataloguing impossible goods while noting her god's decade of silence with a merchant's cold precision. A junior clerk begs her to look at an old acquisition: a prophecy book whose newest entry bears tonight's date—and her name. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys tests the prophecy book against every authentication rite the guild owns; it predates its own paper. The entry describes her standing in a burning hall swearing a false oath. Guildmaster Corvane orders the book sealed and Emrys watched. She copies the page anyway. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: defiance kindling under obedience.

chapters.title: The Date Arrives
chapters.summary: At moonrise the prophecy activates: the ledger hall ignites exactly as written, and Emrys is pulled through the smoke into the throne room of Castle Veyra, mid-prophecy, mid-sentence. Guards see her appear from nothing. Above the throne, King Aldric sits glassy-eyed while something behind his eyes watches her back. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into grim purpose.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Emrys witnesses the Regent speak through Aldric, offering her guild contracts for her silence. She plays the mercenary, negotiating while mapping the palace's wards. Captain Sera Dain, the one guard who flinched at the king's wrongness, quietly signals she wants to talk. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: predatory caution becoming alliance.

chapters.title: Sera's Oath, Broken Smaller
chapters.summary: Sera reveals she swore an oath to protect the king and can feel the Regent rewriting her memories nightly; she keeps a hidden journal to remember herself. Comparing journals, the women discover the Regent feeds on sworn loyalty—it eats oaths. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: lonely fear finding a witness.

chapters.title: What the God Swallowed
chapters.summary: Emrys prays to her silent god out of habit and receives, for the first time in ten years, a single word: RUN. Interrogating the word, she realizes her god didn't go silent—it was silenced, and the Regent may be what did the silencing. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grief reframed as betrayal.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Vanguard
chapters.summary: Word arrives that General Mavros, claiming Aldric dead and himself rightful heir, marches on the free cities with armies fed on captured oath-sworn soldiers. The council panics; the Regent, through Aldric, proposes a horrifying treaty that would feed the cities' oaths to it in exchange for 'peace.' POV: Councilor Ives. Emotional beat: dread of two monsters choosing between them.

chapters.title: Ledger Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Emrys does what she does best: accounting. She calculates the Regent's consumption rate from Sera's journal and realizes it must feed again within nine days or weaken enough to be unbound—but the feeding will be a public oath ceremony that will enslave thousands. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: cold clarity hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Chapel
chapters.summary: Following the god's second word—DIG—Emrys and Sera find a sealed archive beneath the castle chapel containing records from a century ago: the prophecy book's twin volume, and evidence the Regent was bound once before by a god's sacrifice. The binding required an oathbreaker willing to be forgotten. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by terrible terms.

chapters.title: The First Oathbreaker
chapters.summary: The archive names the original binder: Saint Verity, who shattered the Regent a century ago by breaking every oath she held and letting memory itself consume her. The prophecy book was her diary. Emrys understands why her name is in it: she is meant to be the next sacrifice. POV: Emrys via Verity's diary entries. Emotional beat: horror of being chosen.

chapters.title: Corvane Knows
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane arrives at court, revealing the guild has known about the Regent for a century and has been grooming oathbreakers as contingency stock—including Emrys, whose mercenary contract was engineered to make her breakable. Her loyalty to the guild was itself a leash. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into fury.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Glass
chapters.summary: Mavros's army arrives early; the Regent accelerates the oath ceremony to three days. The city's temples begin emptying as sworn soldiers feel their loyalties thinning. Sera's journal starts writing itself in someone else's hand. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: time collapsing, trust eroding.

chapters.title: A Bargain with a Silent Partner
chapters.summary: Emrys offers her god a trade: her accumulated decade of unanswered prayers—all the faith she banked—as fuel to reach inside the Regent and speak to Aldric directly. The god answers with a vision: it has been imprisoned inside the Regent all along, screaming. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: devastating reunion with a caged god.

chapters.title: The King Underneath
chapters.summary: Through the vision-bridge, Emrys reaches Aldric, still alive inside his own body, keeping himself sane by reciting the names of everyone he's failed. He asks her not to save him if saving him costs the city. She refuses the terms and promises both. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: dignity in captivity, stubborn compassion.

chapters.title: The Ceremony of Chains
chapters.summary: Day one of the oath ceremony: ten thousand citizens swear renewed fealty, and the Regent visibly strengthens, glass spreading across Aldric's skin. Emrys sabotages the ward-lattice but Corvane exposes her to the court as a prophecy-marked assassin. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: public ruin, private certainty.

chapters.title: Every Chain Has Two Ends
chapters.summary: Imprisoned, Emrys turns her interrogation of Corvane into a reversal: she proves the guild's own founding charter is an oath to the imprisoned god, meaning the guild itself is bound to help her—or dissolve. Corvane, cornered by his own paperwork, releases her. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: triumph of the ledger over the master.

chapters.title: The Night of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Emrys raids the guild's vault for bottled years and spent oaths, arming herself with other people's discarded promises. Sera rallies the still-unsworn guards. They plan to interrupt day three's ceremony at the moment of maximum feeding, when the Regent's grip loosens. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: desperate courage, found family.

chapters.title: Day Three: The Breaking of the Host
chapters.summary: The climax begins: mid-ceremony, Emrys pours a century of bottled years into Aldric, giving him strength to fight from within while she attacks the Regent's lattice from without. The god, channeled through her, speaks aloud for the first time in a decade—and the sound cracks the glass. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: everything wagered at once.

chapters.title: The Price of the Unbinding
chapters.summary: The Regent, dying, offers Emrys the one thing she wants: restoration of her god's voice, if she swears a new oath and becomes its next host. Remembering Verity's fate, Emrys instead breaks her founding oath deliberately—unmaking the guild's claim on her—and the resulting vacuum tears the Regent apart. The god spends its last strength sealing the rupture. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, grief and freedom entwined.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence
chapters.summary: The god is truly gone now—not silenced but spent—and Emrys feels the absence like an amputation. Aldric, freed but fragile, must convince a battered city he is himself. Mavros's army, its oath-fed soldiers suddenly ownerless, wavers at the walls. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: hollow victory, the long work of being believed.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Free Cities
chapters.summary: Rather than fight, Emrys reads Mavros's own conscription ledgers aloud over the walls—every soldier hears the exact terms of the oath they never knew they'd signed. Half desert; the rest turn on Mavros when the Regent's taint in his command seal is exposed. Truth, weaponized gently, wins where steel would have bled the city dry. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: vindication of her creed—paper cuts deeper than swords.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Months later, Emrys reopens the guild under new charter: no more impossible trades, only the honest recording of oaths made and kept. Sera commands the rebuilt guard; Aldric reigns, remembering his failures by choice. On the last page of the new ledger, Emrys writes a debt forgiven—her own—to a silent god, and finally mourns. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: quiet peace, memory honored, loyalty redefined.
